title: Gabon calculator readiness — Batch 50
scope: Official INSTAT EPVA statistical tables were extracted for cassava and plantain by province. This is a research evidence addition, not authorization to activate Gabon or change calculator formulas.

source.name: INSTAT Gabon, Recensement Général de l’Agriculture 2022–2023, Enquête de Productions Végétale et Animale, Volume 2 — Tableaux statistiques
tables: Tableau 119: average yield (t/ha) by province for cassava and plantain
Tableau 120: cassava area, yield and production by province
Tableau 121: plantain area, yield and production by province
source.source_note: The PDF is Volume 2, statistical tables. The EPVA page states the survey supplements the RGA enumeration and is intended to measure agricultural production and agripastoral activity.

national_totals.caveat: Totals are transcribed from EPVA Tables 120 and 121. Province rows and totals should be checked against the original PDF before production use; some table 119 yield entries appear even where table 121 shows no area/production.

additional_data_coverage.other_epva_tables: The volume also contains province-level tables on farm labour types and days/hours worked, crop and parcel practices, seed acquisition and quality, fertilizer and crop-protection use, livestock populations and equipment. These are structural/use indicators, not current unit prices or monetary enterprise budgets.

findings: Cassava and plantain are the main food crops; maize production is small.
Above-average rainfall and flooding in the first half of 2026 may have affected the secondary maize crop.
2026 cereal import requirements forecast at 255,000 tonnes; cereals account for about 90 percent of utilization.

current_context.source: Gabonese Press Agency citing DGEPF sector note
findings: Cash-crop production index fell 12.4 percent in Q4 2025; palm bunch harvest fell 26.4 percent in the quarter.
Wet rubber production increased 21.4 percent in Q4 2025.

current_context.source: Gabonese Press Agency citing DGEPF sector note
findings: Cash-crop activity increased 42.2 percent quarter-on-quarter in Q2 2026, with palm bunch harvest up 82.2 percent from Q1.
This is an industrial cash-crop index, not smallholder food-crop yield or farmgate price data.

blockers: Transcribe and validate the complete EPVA crop and livestock tables, including source-period and sampling metadata; resolve table 119 versus Tables 120–121 plantain province inconsistencies.
Extract province-level crop data for other supported commodities where EPVA provides observations; do not extrapolate cassava/plantain yields to other crops.
Obtain dated province-level farmgate prices by commodity, grade, unit and market level.
Obtain current farmer-paid seed, fertilizer, crop-protection, irrigation, energy, labour, machinery, transport, packaging and storage costs.
Construct province-specific enterprise budgets and test cases before mapping any data into the calculator.
decision: Gabon remains research-only. EPVA now provides a meaningful province-level cassava and plantain evidence base, but the missing farmgate prices and operating costs prevent calculator activation.
